title: From a sales bottleneck to a live AI pilot
description: How Authentia defined and built an AI-assisted lead qualification pilot for a dental technology supplier, with a limited live rollout in Canada.
summary: Use-case definition, workflow design, technology selection, and development for a Canadian pilot, with a broader US rollout planned.
answer: Authentia handled use-case definition, workflow design, tool selection, and development for a dental technology lead qualification pilot. The solution reached a selected group of clients in Canada and received strongly positive qualitative feedback. A broader US rollout is planned.
author: Authentia
body:
A sales enquiry about dental technology can involve equipment, software, workflow, and specialist knowledge. This engagement focused on the first stages of that conversation: understanding a prospect's needs and connecting them with the right follow-up.

The business problem

Buying dental technology involves detailed questions. A dental laboratory evaluating production equipment has different needs from a practice considering a new digital workflow. Prospects may want to understand compatibility, software, training, materials, or how a product fits into work they already do.

The supplier's sales process involved reviewing inbound enquiries, following up, understanding the prospect's needs, and arranging a conversation with the right person. Those steps contained useful information and human judgement, alongside repetitive coordination. The opportunity was to explore whether an AI-assisted first conversation could help a prospect make progress while preserving access to a specialist.

That gave the engagement a specific business focus: the journey between an enquiry and a qualified discovery meeting. It also created a manageable boundary for a pilot, with a clear place for the sales team to enter the conversation.

Defining a useful role for AI

The proposed assistant needed to work with the supplier's actual product context. An enquiry about equipment could lead to questions about software and workflow. A conversation about components could require a different qualification path. The design therefore accounted for the distinction between dental laboratories and practices, and for the product knowledge needed to make the initial exchange useful.

We scoped an assistant that could ask relevant qualification questions, respond using the supplied product knowledge, and help arrange a meeting. Specialist escalation remained part of the workflow when a conversation required deeper expertise. This was a commercial enquiry workflow; its purpose was to support product discovery and sales conversations.

The design work connected the conversation to a concrete next step. A useful answer alone would leave coordination unfinished. Qualification, scheduling, and confirmation therefore formed part of the same pilot scope.

The workflow we designed

  1. Capture the enquiry. A prospect's details and interests enter through a form, with a CSV import option included in the pilot scope.
  2. Start a product-informed conversation. The assistant uses a knowledge base built around the supplier's offering and the questions its buyers ask.
  3. Qualify the opportunity. The conversation gathers context about the prospect's needs and helps distinguish the appropriate next step.
  4. Bring in specialist judgement. Questions requiring deeper expertise are directed toward a human specialist.
  5. Arrange the follow-up. Scheduling and confirmation connect the initial enquiry with a discovery meeting.

This workflow provided a shared description of what the pilot was intended to do. It connected the customer-facing interaction with the information and coordination needed behind it.

Keeping the pilot focused

We defined an initial scope that could be evaluated before expanding the system's responsibilities. Broader CRM integration was positioned as a later step, beyond the initial pilot. Scheduling requirements were considered within the pilot design without making the entire existing sales environment part of the first release.

That boundary mattered. A pilot can become difficult to interpret when it attempts to replace too many processes at once. Here, the initial journey gave the client a focused way to experience the assistant with a selected group of clients, while keeping broader integration and rollout decisions visible as subsequent work.

Our contribution covered opportunity definition, workflow design, technology selection, development, and preparation for the pilot rollout. The engagement brought business understanding and technical work together: the proposed experience had to make sense to the sales team and be expressed clearly enough to build.

A limited live rollout in Canada

The solution was rolled out to a selected group of clients in Canada. Feedback from that pilot was strongly positive. A larger rollout in the United States is planned.

What this experience brings to our advisory work

This engagement illustrates the decisions that sit between an AI idea and a usable pilot: choosing a bounded workflow, defining the knowledge the system needs, identifying where specialists remain involved, and deciding which integrations belong in the first phase.

For leaders considering a similar opportunity, those decisions are a useful place to start. A clear scope gives a delivery team something concrete to implement and gives the business a basis for deciding what to evaluate next. Authentia's advisory work draws on this practical implementation experience to help clients shape their own opportunities, briefs, and pilot decisions.

title: Modernizing a digital banking experience
description: Selected digital delivery experience supporting the redesign of a financial institution's banking platform through product, design, and engineering collaboration.
summary: Product, design, and engineering collaboration on a banking platform modernization, informing Authentia's practical approach to technology decisions.
answer: This earlier digital delivery engagement supported a financial institution's banking platform modernization through product management, user research, design, engineering, and coordination. It shows the implementation experience behind Authentia's advisory perspective, with the case focused on conventional software delivery.
author: Authentia
body:
Modernizing an established banking platform means connecting the experience customers see with the technology and collaboration behind it. This engagement brought product, design, and engineering perspectives to a financial institution's digital service.

A familiar service with a changing digital experience

Banking products bring demanding expectations together. Customers want to understand what they can do, move through familiar tasks, and trust the service they are using. The institution wanted to improve its existing platform's usability, security, and ability to evolve, within delivery and budget constraints.

That made the work a product challenge as well as a technical one. An interface could only improve the experience if it connected with the underlying platform and reflected the way customers needed to use the service. Design and development therefore had to be considered together.

Connecting research, design, and development

Authentia brought together product, design, engineering, and coordination experience to support the redesign. User research informed the work, while an iterative development approach provided a way to bring the platform's requirements into the delivery process.

The resulting focus was a banking experience that could work across devices and support the institution's continuing digital needs. Collaboration with the client's stakeholders was central to the engagement. Product expectations, experience design, and implementation details needed a shared direction.

The work required attention to several connected considerations:

  • Usability. The platform needed to make its functions accessible and understandable to the people using it.
  • Consistency. Customers could encounter the banking service through different devices, so the experience needed to remain coherent.
  • Security. Changes to a financial service had to be considered alongside the trust and protection expected of the platform.
  • Evolution. The redesigned platform needed to support ongoing development as the institution's digital offering changed.

A delivery contribution with a clear context

Authentia's contribution sat within a conventional digital product engagement. The project involved modernizing a banking platform through research, design, development, and collaboration. It is part of our digital delivery track record.

The redesigned experience provided the institution with an updated platform across devices. The engagement also reinforced the importance of connecting the people who define a product's intended experience with the people responsible for making that experience work.

Why this background matters to AI decisions

Introducing AI into an established business raises many of the same questions about users, systems, and ownership. Leaders need to understand what will change in an existing process, how that change will be experienced, and who will be responsible when a decision or exception needs attention.

Our experience with digital products helps us approach those questions concretely. A recommendation needs to account for the environment in which it will operate, including the user journey, existing technology, stakeholder expectations, and delivery constraints. Those considerations shape a useful implementation brief before a project begins.

This perspective supports our current advisory work: helping clients connect a business objective with a practical path for their own delivery teams and partners.

title: Supporting a cross-border vehicle marketplace
description: Selected digital delivery experience supporting a vehicle marketplace connecting private sellers and dealerships across Canada and the United States.
summary: Delivery coordination and engineering collaboration for a marketplace spanning mobile, web, bidding, and third-party services.
answer: Authentia supported development of a vehicle marketplace connecting private sellers and dealerships across Canada and the United States. The contribution centred on engineering collaboration and delivery coordination within the client's wider leadership structure. This is earlier digital product experience.
author: Authentia
body:
A vehicle transaction crosses several journeys: listing, bidding, offer acceptance, and the steps that follow. Supporting a marketplace built around that process meant working across mobile, web, and connected services.

One transaction, several connected journeys

The product brought together people with different needs. A vehicle owner needed a way to submit information and review offers. A dealership needed to assess a listing and participate in bidding. Once an offer was accepted, the platform needed to connect that decision with the subsequent transaction.

The intended experience joined mobile and web applications with real-time bidding, vehicle information, agreements, payment-related services, and logistics coordination. A change in one part of that journey could affect the work that followed it. The complexity lay in connecting the parts into a coherent product.

A practical delivery contribution

Authentia supported the engineering work and its coordination across the engagement. The broader client-side leadership retained ownership of product strategy and project direction. Our contribution focused on supporting the development effort and collaboration needed to bring the product's requirements into implementation.

The work spanned the consumer-facing mobile experience and the dealership-facing web environment. The documented product scope covered the following journey:

  1. Vehicle submission. A seller provides the information needed to present a vehicle for bidding.
  2. Dealership bidding. Participating dealerships review listings and submit bids through the platform.
  3. Offer review and acceptance. The seller considers an offer and proceeds through the application.
  4. Transaction coordination. Connected services support agreements, payment-related steps, and collection or drop-off arrangements.

Working across product boundaries

The platform combined application development with third-party integrations. Vehicle history, contract execution, and transaction-related services needed to fit into the wider journey. Mobile and web interfaces also needed to work with shared platform services and data.

This kind of delivery depends on understanding the boundaries between systems. The customer sees a continuous experience, while the implementation crosses applications and service providers. Coordinating the work requires attention to those connections as well as to the individual features.

The marketplace also served participants in Canada and the United States. That cross-border context formed part of the product's operational requirements and the environment in which its integrations needed to work.

Experience through launch and further development

The marketplace was developed and launched, with continuing work on maintenance and additional features following the initial release. Authentia's earlier delivery experience includes that transition from building a product to supporting its ongoing development.

This case reflects conventional software delivery. It demonstrates experience with connected customer journeys, application development, integration dependencies, and collaboration within an established project structure.

What it contributes to our advisory perspective

An AI recommendation eventually meets an existing system. Information has to enter somewhere, outputs need to reach the next person or process, and someone has to own the exceptions. Experience with integrated digital products helps us recognize those practical dependencies when discussing a new opportunity.

That is useful when a client is deciding what belongs in a pilot, what can remain in existing tools, and what a delivery partner needs to understand. Clear boundaries and responsibilities make a brief more useful to the people implementing it.

Authentia brings that implementation context to its current strategy and advisory engagements, helping business leaders prepare decisions that their teams and technology partners can act on.
